subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — P2P timelines, term options, and CFO signoff question
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer request — pricing, term options, and procurement timing

Connor,

Thanks for taking the call this morning. To help procurement and finance size the ask, can you send a private offer breakdown with:
- Pricing for 12-month annual commitment vs 12-month usage (pay-as-you-go) — please include list and effective unit rates (tokens/hr or per-invocation guidance).
- Any recommended term splits (e.g., pilot + annual conversion) that speed approvals.
- Required buyer approvals on your side (do we need CFO-level approval or is procurement + legal sufficient?).
- Evidence pack: SOC 2 report, SLA addendum, and any activation checklist we should attach to the PO.
- Typical PO lead times and activation window from PO receipt to marketplace activation (ideally broken into procurement and activation steps).

We have a target go-live for a 30-day pilot starting mid-September; financing may prefer staging costs across two invoices. Also flag anything that triggers an internal CFO exception (we need to know now if a formal exception request will be required).

Appreciate if you can get the initial package by EOD Monday so procurement can triage.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
VP, Product
AcmeHealth

--
Attachment: none (will accept your evidence links)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer request — pricing, term options, and procurement timing

Laura — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (pricing), Marcus (co-sell/marketplace ops), and Neha (activation/process) to pull the package. Quick sketch of how we can structure this to minimize CFO friction: 

1) Two-step option (recommended):
   - Phase 1: 30-day pilot (usage-based) with capped spend (recommend $25k cap) to validate integration.
   - Phase 2: 11-month committed annual with reduced unit-rate — converts on PO receipt for the remainder of the year.

2) Single-PO annual option: standard 12-month private offer with an SLA addendum; may require CFO approval if total committed spend > $500k (we'll flag).

3) Evidence: Vanessa to share SOC2 & SLA addendum; Marcus will provide the PO template and marketplace activation checklist. Neha will confirm marketplace activation latency (typical 3–5 business days after PO + signing).

Action items: Vanessa — can you draft the two pricing scenarios and attach SOC2/SLA? Marcus — please add PO template + activation checklist to the thread. Neha — confirm activation timing and the buyer-approval gates we need to request from Acme (procurement vs finance).

I can join procurement call if needed Monday morning.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0142

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmehealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer request — pricing, term options, and procurement timing

Hi all — attaching the packet below and putting proposed numbers on the table so procurement has something to review. I copied Marcus and Neha for activation steps and can help shepherd a CFO/finance exception if needed.

Summary (two recommended options):

Option A — Pilot + Commit (recommended)- Pilot: 30-day usage cap $25,000 (no long-term commitment)- Annual commit (post-pilot): $240,000 annual spend (monthly invoiced or annual invoice) — effective price ~20% discount vs usage

Option B — Straight 12-month private offer- 12-month commit: $300,000 annual spend (best price tier, requires standard marketplace activation)

Notes on approvals:
- Procurement + Legal: sufficient for PO issuance in most cases.
- CFO signoff: required if annual spend > $500k OR if customer asks for custom payment terms beyond Net-30 / invoice schedule. For Acme, neither option crosses $500k, so CFO escalation unlikely.

Activation timeline:
- Receipt of signed PO / signed DocuSign: marketplace activation in 3–5 business days.
- If customer requests managed onboarding or dedicated capacity, add 2–3 weeks.

Attachments (stubs):
- SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (SOC 2 Type II report — redacted)
- SLA-Addendum_Acme.docx (standard SLA addendum with uptime and support tiers)
- PO-Template_Acme.xlsx (PO template you can paste into your procurement system)

HubSpot / Docs: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1427 (deal record)

Marcus will confirm the marketplace activation checklist below. If this all looks good, Connor — suggest we send the DocuSign + PO template by EOD so procurement can route.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Commercial Ops Manager | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (attached, redacted stub), SLA-Addendum_Acme.docx (attached), PO-Template_Acme.xlsx (attached)

Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer request — pricing, term options, and procurement timing

Connor / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Procurement reviewed Option A and prefers the pilot + commit structure (Option A) to limit risk. A few clarifying items before we issue the PO: 

1) Can you confirm the billing cadence you recommend for the annual convert (monthly invoice vs annual invoice)? We prefer monthly billing if possible.
2) We confirm the pilot cap at $25k; please confirm whether usage overage during pilot is billed or simply blocked.
3) Please send the DocuSign link for the SLA addendum + private-offer acceptance so our legal can review signatures.

Assuming the above, procurement will aim to issue a PO by next Thursday 9/2. Activation target still 3–5 business days after PO acceptance.

Laura — I'll schedule a quick review with finance (CFO on standby if they ask, but looks under the $500k threshold).

Procurement Manager (on behalf of AcmeHealth)
AcmeHealth — Strategic Sourcing
